title: the WSG movement on slippery horizontal surfaces
audit_label: R447 WSG slippery surface movement pin audit
audit_comment: The slippery surface slice pins the full-rate straight-line rule (no fall risk in a straight line at the full normal movement rate), the Dexterity Check on anything other than a very gradual turn or an abrupt stop or speed-up, the running rule (a Dexterity Check after every five segments of running, even in a straight line), the half-rate exemption (turns need no check at half the full normal movement rate), the full-round speed-change exemption (a full round to slow down or speed up, full movement to standstill or vice versa, needs no check), and the fall consequence (no direct damage, only an indirect cause of greater problems) (rules/wsgslip.h, prefix wsl); census 371 -> 372.

banner.title: The WSG MOVEMENT ON SLIPPERY HORIZONTAL SURFACES, R447: the slippery prose (no table this round) - a character who does not exercise caution when traveling across a slippery horizontal surface risks slipping and falling down, which does not directly cause him to suffer damage but could be an indirect cause of greater problems to come. He can move at his full normal movement rate without risking a fall IF he travels in a straight line; anything other than a very gradual turn, or an abrupt stop or speed-up, demands a successful Dexterity Check to avoid slipping and falling down. A character attempting to RUN must make a Dexterity Check after every five segments of such movement to stay on his feet, even in a straight line. At only HALF his full normal movement rate he can turn with no check; and taking a full round to slow down or speed up (full normal movement to a standstill, or vice versa) needs no check. Census 371 -> 372.
banner.provenance: the WSG scan (archive.org item pdfy-B3Fz83tZ3TV7zOc8), printed p. 39; the user own copy OCR cross-checked against the archive djvu word layer (Guide_0039.djvu) - the section reads CLEAN, every number (the five-segment running check cadence, the half-rate cautious turn, the full-round speed change) matched exactly; no eye-reads were needed.
banner.sentinel: Straight-line travel at the full rate is free; every other movement choice costs a Dexterity check - a turn, an abrupt stop or speed-up, or a run with its check every five segments - unless the character drops to half rate for the turn or spends a full round on the speed change, and the fall itself does no direct damage.

consts.name: wslRunCheckSegs
consts.comment: If a character attempts to run on a slippery surface, he must make a Dexterity Check after every five segments of this sort of movement to stay on his feet, even if he is traveling in a straight line.

consts.name: wslCautiousRateDiv
consts.comment: By moving at only half of his full normal movement rate (the rate divided by 2), a character can turn without needing to make a Dexterity Check.

bools.name: wslCautionRisksFall
bools.comment: A character who does not exercise caution when traveling across a slippery horizontal surface risks slipping and falling down.

bools.name: wslStraightFullRateSafe
bools.comment: A character can move at his full normal movement rate across a slippery surface without risking a fall, if he travels in a straight line.

bools.name: wslAbruptChangeNeedsDexCheck
bools.comment: If he attempts anything other than a very gradual turn, or if he tries to stop or speed up abruptly, he must make a successful Dexterity Check to avoid slipping and falling down.

bools.name: wslRunCheckEvenStraight
bools.comment: A character attempting to run on a slippery surface makes the every-five-segments Dexterity Check even if he is traveling in a straight line.

bools.name: wslFullRoundSpeedChangeFree
bools.comment: If he takes a full round to slow down or speed up - from full normal movement to a standstill, or vice versa - then no Dexterity Check is required.

bools.name: wslFallNoDirectDamage
bools.comment: Slipping and falling down does not directly cause the character to suffer damage, but could be an indirect cause of greater problems to come.
